feature: Ask runs on Qwen3.8 27B by default
summary: Ask's built-in model is now Qwen3.8 27B at 4-bit, with its small draft model so it writes about twice as fast, on any Mac with 48 GB or more. A Mac that already has Qwen3.6 35B keeps using it, is offered the new one in Settings with its size, and can delete the old one once both are down.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Settings > Ask. The model files go in Application Support > Photonz > Models.

try.do: On a Mac that has only Qwen3.6 35B, open Settings (Command-comma) and find Ask: Qwen3.6 35B is still the model, and Qwen3.8 27B is offered beside it with its size.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Download on the New default row and wait for 21.3 GB.
Look at Model: it now reads Automatic (Qwen3.8 27B), and Qwen3.6 35B has a Delete.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Delete beside Qwen3.6 35B: it asks first and says it frees 21.0 GB.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: On a Mac with no model yet, Settings > Ask offers Qwen3.8 27B, 21.3 GB, and still offers the picture model under it.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Open a screenshot, press Ask and type: annotate the ux with measurements around the major ui elements. Time it, then ask a second thing straight after and time that.

evaluate: Is waiting about a minute and a half for the first answer after Ask loads acceptable for now, given that a second request right after is quick?
Do Qwen3.8's sheets, titles and zooms look better to you than the 35B's did (it scored higher there)?
Is 'New default: Qwen3.8 27B (21.3 GB)' with a Download button clear enough, or should the old model's row say more?
Should Delete also be offered for the model in use, falling back to the next one?
rough: Measured on this M4 Max, 64 GB, same code (commit 2abd8391 plus this change), every case from a cold start. Climb set (41 cases): Qwen3.8 27B 75.3 (drawing 79.4, sheet 81.4, layout 67.9, redline 46.6, video 54), 140.8 s median a request, 24.4 GB held median and 27.6 peak (run 20261024-131153-ask). Qwen3.6 35B 77.1 (86.3, 65.2, 32.9, 48.3, 37.8), 52.1 s, 21.8 median and 23.5 peak (20261024-151759-ask).

Held-out set (45 cases): Qwen3.8 27B 57.8 (drawing 64.4, layout 12.3, redline 22.3, video 59.6), 141.9 s median, 27.0 GB peak (20261024-163432-ask-held-out). Qwen3.6 35B 60.2 (68.4, 22.4, 9.2, 50.1), 49.1 s, 23.8 GB peak (20261024-191502-ask-held-out). Nothing looked up in either.

Slower: about three times the 35B's time a request. Qwen3.8 is dense and reads a prompt at 103 to 183 tokens a second here against the 35B's 1,046, so a cold first request spends 60 to 90 s reading Ask's instructions. Screenshot measurements take 83 s against 14 s. A warm second request reads only what is new (1.6 s against 62.8 s on the same 12,500-token prompt). Filed as ask-s-first-answer-after-its-model-loads-comes-i.

Worse on drawings: climb 79.4 against 86.3, held-out 64.4 against 68.4. Two climb drawings ended with 'I couldn't make a clear drawing of that' because Qwen3.8, checking its own drawing, would not accept a blue tit or a plain bird as 'a bird on a branch singing'. Filed as ask-on-qwen3-8-27b-keeps-a-drawing-its-look-name.
Worse on held-out layout: 12.3 against 22.4. Folded into ask-on-the-local-model-makes-results-that-look-f, whose bar is that group.
Better on sheets (81.4 against 65.2), video (54 against 37.8 climb, 59.6 against 50.1 held-out) and held-out redline (22.3 against 9.2).

The draft (mtp-Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_0.gguf, 1.7 GB, llama.cpp's multi-token prediction) is kept: on 8 climb cases 73.8 with it against 60.4 without (run 20261024-160940-ask), because without it the component table and the pricing section ran past the eval's 300 s. Writing a 700-token svg: 11.9 tokens a second without, 33.2 with MTP, 28.7 with the DFlash draft. Short requests take about the same time either way. It costs about 3.8 GB more memory.

The vendored server stays at llama.cpp b11826: it loads Qwen3.8 (same architecture as Qwen3.6 27B), answers tool calls and reads pictures. The newest build, b11853, measured the same speed back to back (132 against 135 tokens a second reading).

The memory rule now gives Qwen3.8 27B to a 48 GB Mac and up, Qwen3.6 35B to a 40 GB Mac, Gemma 4 26B to a 36 GB Mac. The picture model is still offered beside Qwen3.8 on a 64 GB Mac (24.4 + 12 GB inside the three-fifths share).
The Delete in the walk is pressed by name, not clicked at a point: the walk's pointer click reaches only the editor window. They are plain Settings buttons with nothing laid over them.

The eval had been reporting 0 GB held for every built-in run: it read the server's small shell watch instead of the server. It now reads the biggest of them, which is how the memory numbers above were taken.
